items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: Quick take on Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow - (1) What on earth is Kushner doing representing the United States? What position does he hold? What is his legitimacy? Not enough is said about how egregious this is. (2) Witkoff's sucking up to Putin a good demonstration of what the collapse of US state capacity looks like. It's not just embarrassing, but illustrates a trend of democratic decline. (3) Putin could only be open to stopping the war in 2026 if he were quite a different person - this would require him being willing to take a deal he hates in order to partially reintegrate with the West and try to undermine it from within. (4) Putin is currently focused on winter, when he can deprive Ukrainians of heat and water, and hope they re-conceive of war as weather, and turn on each other. The psychological component is key to Putin's winter strategy. (5) Whatever is happening with mobilisation after the parliamentary election later this month, it is front of mind for Putin. Mobilisation is as much a regime security as a national security decision for him. (6) Putin remains confident that he can win in the long run. He hopes Ukraine will sink into political crisis, and authoritarian pro-Putin leaders will take power in France, the UK and Germany. Time, he thinks, is still on his side. (7) The crises Russia faces do not, in Putin's mind, translate into a short-term threat to his power. Therefore, they are not existential. (8) It's a brick wall without chinks - for now, Putin is not open to stopping the war. (9) This is infuriating for Trump, not only because he can't get his way, but because he can't grasp why he can't get his way. In Trump's mind, his personal connection with Putin, his elevation of Putin into a fantasy society to which he and Putin belong, should be enough to secure a deal.

Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi said Zaits was chosen for his command experience, ability to deliver results and adoption of new technologies. His priorities include realistic training, merit-based leadership, rapid integration of battlefield lessons and technologies that provide combat advantages while reducing risks to troops. #Ukraine

Putin posthumously awarded Chernyshev the Order of Courage. #Ukraine

items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: I interpret the last 10-14 days as a contest over who gets to define reality before negotiations resume. Ratcliffe went to Moscow saying, effectively - You are weaker than you think. Negotiate before it gets worse. Putin’s response appears to be - Watch what we can still do. Intensifying strikes immediately afterward is Moscow working to demonstrate that it retains escalation capacity. Moscow knew that flying Witkoff and Kushner directly into Kyiv was under consideration, hitting the relevant airports is a remarkably unsubtle way of saying - Russia controls the escalation environment in which diplomacy occurs. It also forces the Americans back into the familiar rail and ground-security architecture rather than allowing a highly symbolic American aircraft arrival in wartime Kyiv. That symbolism would have mattered enormously. An American delegation flying into Kyiv would implicitly demonstrate that Russia can be compelled, or at least induced, to tolerate protected air movement into the Ukrainian capital. That starts looking close to an air ceasefire or a protected corridor. Preventing that has strategic value for Moscow. The strike against SBU HQ is more of the same - Ratcliffe delivered his message to Bortnikov. Russia struck the office of Bortnikov’s Ukrainian counterpart. Time will tell, but I think we are entering a dangerous new phase of the war. A two week power shot/ranking would unfortunately look like this: Russia: ↑↑ - seized the psychological initiative, escalated successfully, projecting confidence Ukraine: → / slight ↑ - under enormous air pressure and frontline strain, but battlefield performance and deep-strike capability are considerably strong United States: ↓↓ - enormous latent leverage, but currently displaying considerably more desire for an agreement than Russia and therefore allowing Putin to keep testing Trump A significant American or European coercive move could change this ranking very quickly. Additionally, Zelenskyy proposing a ceasefire and Russia not accepting was a gambit that may have played more successfully in the past. He was rightfully attempting to demonstrate Ukraine is committed to peace. But Putin is working to demonstrate he is committed to winning. I am concerned the latter will convey more strength.

Spannende Analyse der Lage bei Pokrowsk:
❗️Offenbar geben die russischen Offiziere ihren Sturmtruppen die extrem geschönten russischen Karten mit auf den Weg.
➡️Diese wundern sich dann, wenn sie mitten im „befreiten“ Gebiet in feste ukrainische Positionen rennen.🤦🏻‍♂️
#lesenswert
Rubizh (@RubizhBrigade)
What the hell is going on at POKROVSK direction??
Russian invaders seem to be pooling reserves for further advances. As usual, they are trying to infiltrate as deeply as possible into residential areas. Or what's left of them.
We don't make it easy for them. Every day we "decommission" anywhere from 3 to 20 enemy soldiers.
Fun fact - many POWs we take near our strongpoints claim they were told that the area had no Ukrainian presence. Basically, Russian command lies to their soldiers, and sends them on a suicide-scouting-infiltrating missions.
At the same time, they really want our logistics gone. Hence the drone spam. Last Sunday, we had about 300(!) enemy drones in our are of responsibility. Usually, smoking out the infiltrated Russian infantry isn't that big of an issue. But it is a lot harder once you also have to dodge enemy drones on your search-and-destroy missions.
Interestingly, Russians had also pulled their artillery closer to the frontline. Perhaps, they find that their current pace of advance unacceptable and feel like risking their artillery. Suffice to say - we've got plenty of boring videos of our drone pilots blowing them to kingdom come.
Cherry on top - while our logistics are a nightmare, so it is for the Russians. They have to lug all their equipment and supplies primarily on foot, just as we do.
After all, two can play at the drone-shut-down-the-logistics game :D

items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: BREAKING | 🇺🇸🇷🇺🇺🇦‼️‼️ CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s extraordinary mission to Moscow appears to have backfired, with Vladimir Putin reportedly reading Washington’s attempt to push him toward negotiations not as pressure, but as weakness. According to The Washington Post, Ratcliffe warned Russian intelligence officials that Moscow’s military and economic position would continue to deteriorate if the war dragged on and urged a return to negotiations. Instead, people familiar with the discussions say Putin emerged more determined to pursue a military victory. In the roughly 10 days since the visit, Russia has intensified its jet-powered drone and missile campaign against Ukraine, while Putin has publicly projected confidence that Kyiv can eventually be forced into concessions. The episode exposes a serious weakness in Trump’s current approach to Moscow. Diplomacy without credible consequences can reinforce the Kremlin’s belief that time is on Russia’s side, especially when Putin interprets high-level outreach as evidence that Washington wants a deal more urgently than he does. If the U.S. genuinely wants negotiations to succeed, it must pair them with stronger military support for Ukraine, deeper economic pressure on Russia and a clear cost for continued escalation. Otherwise, Moscow has little incentive to compromise while it still believes more violence can improve its negotiating position. See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo

items.title: RT by @RALee85: Daily Ukraine map thread for Monday 31st August 2026 - End of Month Recent Russian infiltrations through the increasingly sparse Ukrainian lines between Dobropillya and Druzhkivka demonstrate that the Russian command remains intent upon reaching the routes west of Kramatorsk and threatening the communications upon which the defence of the region depends. There have also been several flag-raising incidents around Kharkiv and Sumy. The men raising flags are merely those foolish enough to make themselves visible. The more dangerous infiltrators are those moving in civilian clothing, slipping further behind the lines, locating positions and directing aircraft and drones onto their targets. Despite all this, however, there remains little movement of consequence, and exploitation of weaknesses can go both ways... Beneath this apparent stagnation on the battlefield, the foundations are being laid for a very difficult end to 2026 and into 2027 for Ukraine as a country. We shall ignore the Russian mobilisation rumours and instead focus upon what is known and true thus far. Russia has expanded its production of drones and missiles to a degree which will place enormous pressure upon Ukraine's cities, infrastructure and population. There is much discussion in European capitals of air defence, and rightly so. But there is a hard truth which must be faced: there is not enough air defence in the world to protect Ukraine from what Russia is now capable of producing, let alone what it may produce next year or the year after. In brighter news, Ukraine is no longer in the position it occupied a year ago. Its ability to strike deep into Russian territory has grown enormously this year alone. Refineries, ammunition depots, logistics centres, airfields and military infrastructure which once appeared safely beyond the reach of Ukrainian weapons are now increasingly vulnerable targets. It still does not possess the capabilities to strike Russian missile launch sites in sufficient number, or production sites however, so any talk on this is wishful thinking. The coming winter will be brutal upon the civilian population of Ukraine. But Russia will not pass through it untouched, and the problems facing its forces on the front are compounding with the increase in midstrike, and not going away.
